results.resolved_question: Can you compare information technology and computer engineering in plain english?
results.answer: Information Technology (IT) and Computer Engineering are distinct yet related fields within the broader computing discipline. IT focuses on the design, implementation, and maintenance of technology solutions and support for users of such systems. This involves understanding and managing the technology infrastructure, ensuring it meets user needs and operates efficiently. On the other hand, Computer Engineering is more about the design and construction of processor-based systems, encompassing hardware, software, and communications components. This field requires a deeper understanding of both computer science and electrical engineering, as well as foundational knowledge in mathematics and sciences. [S1] and [S1]

results.answer: For a beginner in their first year, Computer Engineering and Information Technology (IT) differ primarily in their focus and scope. In Computer Engineering, the curriculum typically includes courses that cover the design and construction of processor-based systems, encompassing hardware, software, and communications components. This means that students in Computer Engineering often delve into subjects like computer architecture, digital design, and embedded systems, which are fundamental to understanding how computers work and how they can be designed and built. On the other hand, IT focuses on the design, implementation, and maintenance of technology solutions and support for users of such systems. This includes areas such as network administration, software development, and information security, which are more application-oriented and user-focused. [S1][S2]
